title: Monoidal resolution of characteristic monoids
statement: Let $(X,M)$ be a fine saturated log scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] whose underlying scheme is quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; quasi-compact means every open cover has a finite subcover. Suppose every group $\overline M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}$ is torsion free. Then there exist an integer $n\geq0$ and a finite tower $(X_n,M_n)\to\cdots\to(X_0,M_0)=(X,M)$ of saturated log blowups along nonempty coherent log ideals such that every characteristic monoid $\overline M_{n,\bar x}$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf N^{r(\bar x)}$ for some finite integer $r(\bar x)\geq0$. This assertion requires neither log regularity nor regularity of the strata.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.3.14--Theorem 3.3.15, printed p. 109 and proof pp. 109--110, with the saturated fan desingularization constructed in 3.1.27 and 3.2.19--3.2.21, printed pp. 102 and 105--106. The auxiliary toric resolution is taken over Q; the resulting monoidal construction has no characteristic restriction on X.

mathlib_searches.query: Every quasi compact fine saturated logarithmic scheme has a finite tower of saturated log blowups with free characteristic monoids.
Monoidal desingularization of fine saturated log schemes gives free sharp monoids.
